chunks: Abu al-Hasan al-Rida (peace be upon him) said to me: 'O Yunus! Do not say according to the doctrine of the Qadariyya, for the Qadariyya did not speak according to the speech of the people of Paradise, nor according to the speech of the people of the Fire, nor according to the speech of Iblis.
For the people of Paradise will say: All praise is due to God who guided us to this, and we would not have found guidance had God not guided us. [7:43]
And the people of the Fire will say: Our Lord, our wretchedness overcame us and we were a people gone astray. [23:106]
And Iblis said: My Lord, by what You led me astray. [15:39]

I said: By God! I do not say according to their speech. But I say: nothing can happen except with what God wills, intends, determines, and ordains. So he said: O Yunus! It is not like that. Nothing can happen except what God wills, intends, determines, and ordains.

O Yunus! Do you know what the Desire (mashi'a) is? I said: No. He said: It is the primordial Remembrance (al-dhikr al-awwal). So do you know what the Intention (irada) is? I said: No. He said: It is the determination upon what He desires. So do you know what the Determination (qadar) is? I said: No. He said: It is the Engineering — the placement of limits between subsistence and perishing.
He (the narrator) said: Then he said: And the Ordainment (qada') — it is the sealing and the realization of the concrete reality.
He (the narrator) said: So I sought his permission to kiss his head, and I said: You have opened something for me that I was heedless of.

key_terms.الْإِرَادَة: Irada — the divine Intention; defined as the 'determination upon what is desired' — the specification of the object of the will
key_terms.الْقَدَر: Qadar — the Determination/Measure; defined as the 'Engineering' — setting the blueprint and limits of things between subsistence and perishing
key_terms.الْقَدَرِيَّة: The Qadariyya — a theological sect that held that humans are the sole agents of their actions, denying divine pre-determination
key_terms.الْقَضَاء: Qada' — the Ordainment; the final sealing and realization of things into concrete physical reality (al-'ayn)
key_terms.الْمَشِيئَة: Mashi'a — the divine Will/Desire; here defined as the 'primordial Remembrance' (al-dhikr al-awwal), the first movement in the divine creative process

ai.seo_question: What is the difference between mashi'a, irada, qadar, and qada' in Islamic theology according to Imam al-Ridha?
ai.summary: This hadith records a theological dialogue between Yunus ibn Abd al-Rahman and Imam al-Ridha (AS) on the doctrine of divine decree. The Imam critiques the Qadariyya — a sect that believed humans have independent power over their actions — by showing that even the people of Paradise, the people of Hellfire, and Iblis all attributed their states to God's guidance or God's actions. The Imam then provides precise philosophical definitions of the four stages of divine action: mashi'a (the primordial divine Thought/Remembrance), irada (the Determination/Resolve upon what is willed), qadar (the Engineering — setting limits of duration), and qada' (the sealing and realization of the concrete reality). This dialogue takes place in the context of early Islamic theological debates (2nd–3rd century AH) about free will versus determinism, and the Imam's response represents the Imami Shia position: neither pure determinism (jabr) nor pure free will (qadar), but a nuanced middle position.

en.hubeali:
Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ismail Bin Marrar, from Yunus Bin Abdul Rahman who said, 
‘Abu Al-Hassan Al-Reza<sup>asws</sup> said to me: ‘O Yunus! Do not say with the speech of the Qadiriyya, for the Qadiriyya are not speaking with the speech of the people of the Paradise, nor by the speech of the people of the Fire, nor by the speech of Iblees<sup>la</sup>,
for the people of the Paradise would be saying [7:43] All Praise is due to Allah Who Guided us to this, and we would not have found the Way had it not been that Allah had Guided us;
and the people of the Fire would say [23:106] O our Lord! Our adversity overcame us and we were an erroneous people;
and Ibleesla would say [15:39] He said: Lord! With what You Sent me astray?’.

So I said, ‘By Allahazwj! I am not speaking by their speech, but I am saying, nothing can happen to be except with what Allahazwj so Desires, and Intends, and Determines, and Ordains’. So heasws said: ‘O Yunus! It is not like this. Nothing can happen to be except what Allahazwj so Desires, and Intends, and Determines, and Ordains.

O Yunus! Do you know what is the Desire?’ I said, ‘No’. He<sup style="font-weight: normal">asws</sup> said: ‘It is the first Remembrance (الذِّكْر). So do you know what is the Intention?’ I said, ‘No’. He<sup style="font-weight: normal">asws</sup> said: ‘It is the Determination upon what He<sup style="font-weight: normal">azwj</sup> so Desires. So do you know what is the Determination?’ I said, ‘No’. He<sup style="font-weight: normal">asws</sup> said: ‘It is the Engineering and the Placement of the limitations for the remaining and the perishing’.
He (the narrator) said, ‘Then he<sup style="font-weight: normal">asws</sup> said: ‘And the Ordainment, it is the accomplishment of the eyes (physical reality)’.

He (the narrator) said, ‘So I sought his<sup style="font-weight: normal">asws</sup> permission to kiss his<sup style="font-weight: normal">asws</sup> head, and I said, ‘You<sup style="font-weight: normal">asws</sup> opened something for me which I was oblivious of’.
